sampleSizeCalc

Sample Size Calculator for Clinical Research

A comprehensive R package for sample size determination across 39 design combinations: experimental trials (superiority / non-inferiority / equivalence), observational studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional), diagnostic accuracy studies (estimation, testing, comparison, AUC), and complex designs (cluster RCT, Simon two-stage, bioequivalence, ordered outcomes, prediction models, interrupted time series).

Every result carries: the formula (plain text + LaTeX), precise literature references (section/page level), parameter-role documentation, and methodological hints.

Installation 

devtools::install_github("portos-wang/sampleSizeCalc")
# or from a local source
devtools::install_local("path/to/Sample_Size_Calc")

Quick start: the three-axis API 

library(sampleSizeCalc)

# design x task x outcome
calculate("rct", "test", "mean",
  mean1 = 10, mean2 = 12, sd = 3
)
calculate("rct", "noninferiority", "proportion",
  p1 = 0.90, p2 = 0.85, margin = 0.05
)
calculate("cohort", "test", "proportion",
  p0 = 0.20, p1 = 0.30, ratio = 2, dropout = 0.10
)
calculate("caseControl", "test", "proportion", p0 = 0.3, OR = 2.0)
calculate("diagAccuracy", "estimate", "proportion",
  prob = 0.85, d = 0.05, prevalence = 0.2
)
calculate("diagAUC", "estimate", "auc",
  auc = 0.80, d = 0.10, ratio = 1, var_method = "binormal"
)
calculate("singleArmPhaseII", "test", "proportion",
  p0 = 0.1, p1 = 0.3, optimizer = "optimal"
)
calculate("clusterRCT", "test", "mean",
  mean1 = 10, mean2 = 12, sd = 3, icc = 0.05, cluster_size = 20
)
calculate("bioequivalence", "equivalence", "mean", cv = 0.25)

Unambiguous designs allow omitting task/outcome:

calculate("diagAUC", auc = 0.80, d = 0.05)
calculate("singleProportion", p = 0.30, precision = 0.05)   # -> 323

Illegal combinations error with the list of legal ones. The full design x task x outcome table, formulas, and sources live in docs/DESIGN_MATRIX.md; published worked examples used as numeric test anchors are catalogued in docs/NUMERIC_ANCHORS.md.

Legacy API (silently compatible)

All 17 pre-3.0 keywords keep working with identical results:

sample_size_calculator("twoMeans", mean1 = 10, mean2 = 12, sd = 3)  # 37/group
sample_size_calculator("survival", hr = 0.7)                        # 65 events

Result object

calculate() returns a sample_size_result S3 object with print(), summary() and plot() methods. print() shows the metrics, the role of each parameter under the chosen design, and any methodological hints; summary() adds the formula, LaTeX, precise references and the adjustment audit trail.

Study designs (family overview)

Family Designs
Trials rct (test/NI/superiority/equivalence x mean/proportion/rate/survival), paired (mean/proportion), rctSingleArm, crossover, bioequivalence, singleArmPhaseII (Simon optimal/minimax, A’Hern)
Observational cohort (proportion/rate), caseControl, caseControlMatched, crosstab
Diagnostic diagAccuracy (estimate/test/dual-endpoint), diagAccuracyCompare (test/NI/equivalence), diagAUC, diagAUCCompare (test/NI/equivalence), diagLR
Estimation singleProportion, singleMean, singleCorrelation
Complex clusterRCT, twoOrdinal, predictiveModel, its (experimental)
Deferred kappa, steppedWedge (formula sources under verification)

Literature

Methods are anchored to primary sources, with worked examples from the reference literature used as automated numeric test benchmarks:

  • Zhou, Obuchowski & McClish (2011). Statistical Methods in Diagnostic Medicine (2nd ed.), Wiley - diagnostic module.
  • Machin, Campbell, Tan & Tan (2018). Sample Sizes for Clinical, Laboratory and Epidemiology Studies (4th ed.), Wiley - trial/complex designs.
  • Hajian-Tilaki (2014). J Biomed Informatics 48:193-204 - diagnostic formulas.
  • Akoglu (2022). Turkish J Emergency Medicine 22(4):177-185 - diagnostic comparisons and dual-endpoint strategy.
  • Bhardwaj et al. (2024). J Family Med Prim Care 13(7):2555-2561 - prevalence studies and dropout adjustment.
  • Plus the original methods: Schoenfeld (1983), Fleiss et al. (1980), Casagrande et al. (1978), Schlesselman (1982), Dupont (1988), Connor (1987), Hanley & McNeil (1982/1983), Buderer (1996), Simon (1989), A’Hern (2001), Whitehead (1993), Peduzzi et al. (1996), Schuirmann (1987).

Citation

If you use the package in research, please cite the original methodology papers for each design (listed in every result’s reference field) along with the package:

@software{sampleSizeCalc,
  title = {sampleSizeCalc: Sample Size Calculator for Clinical Research},
  author = {Portos (Yishan) Wang and Bingxin Cai},
  organization = {Gansu Provincial Maternity and Child-care Hospital (Gansu Provincial Central Hospital)},
  year = {2026},
  version = {3.1.0},
  url = {https://github.com/portos-wang/sampleSizeCalc}
}
